tia.docs: Heads-up: opened a PR to add an "Install troubleshooting" appendix for Private/VPC installs. Focused on HSM systemd quirks, Windows service notes for onprem agents, and a tiny Python conn-check snippet for semi-airgapped sites. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4897
oliver.platform: Nice. Can you include a minimal systemd drop-in for the pkcs11 agent? We repeatedly see the plugin failing with permissions on systems with restrictive umask. A short example would help.
ken.sre: Adding a suggested drop-in below, please verify path placeholders are explicit (don't leak real hostnames):
```
# /etc/systemd/system/redwood-hsm.service.d/override.conf
[Service]
Environment=PKCS11_MODULE=/opt/hsm/lib/libpkcs11.so
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5s
LimitNOFILE=65536
# ensure service starts after mounts if the module is on external disk
After=local-fs.target network.target
```
ria: (typo) I mean rachel.sec: Also include Windows instruction to set the pkcs11 module path in the agent config and a note about running the service as a local service account with minimal rights.
rachel.sec: From security: add a plain-language snippet about key-wrap rotation when migrating from managed KMS to HSM. Mention not to perform rotation during maintenance windows without backing up HSM policies. Also: remove any literal example credentials — use placeholders only.
tia.docs: Will remove literals. I'll add a migration section that shows a config diff rather than a full example to avoid secrets. Example diff suggestion:
```diff
- kms: type: managed
- kms: endpoint: kms.redwood.example
+ kms: type: pkcs11
+ kms:
+   pkcs11_module: /opt/hsm/lib/libpkcs11.so
+   slot: 1
+   label: redwood-kms
```
oliver.platform: Perfect. Also, for semi-airgapped conn-check include a minimal egress CIDR list and a tiny Python snippet using our SDK (don't use prod hosts).
ken.sre: Here's the CIDR list we use in staging (example): 203.0.113.0/24:443, 198.51.100.0/24:443. Add DNS fallback note (use internal resolver or Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 if permitted).

# Python conn-check snippet (keeps it small):
```python
# py example: conn-check to private agent endpoint
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(base_url="https://private.local")
status = client.conn_check(host="10.10.0.5", port=443, timeout=5)
print(status)
```
tia.docs: Nice and concise. I'll include that and a short Windows service note: set service user to a local non-admin account and grant 'Log on as a service'.
rachel.sec: Also add an explicit HSM failover checklist: check PKCS11 path, check HSM network connectivity, verify operator role mapping, validate ACLs, and run the automated connection test. Put that as a bulleted list under troubleshooting.
ken.sre: One more SRE tip: call out MTU pitfalls on baremetal and a short command to show kernel dmesg lines if the agent logs show repeated TCP fragmentation. I'll add a one-line example in the checklist.

# Troubleshooting example line:
`dmesg | grep -i mtu`
